# Wall Blocking

Solid wood fitted horizontally between wall studs before drywall goes up, so that a grab bar, shelf or handrail can be screwed into it anywhere later, not just where a stud happens to be.

Why it matters: a grab bar is only as strong as what it is fixed to. Drywall anchors fail under a person's weight. Blocking costs very little with the wall open and a lot once tile is up.

What we did: 2x10 blocking at roughly 33 to 36 inches and in the zones by the toilet and shower entry, in all four walls of the hall bathroom, shaded on the drawings ([[hall-bathroom-design-drawings]]) and photographed with a tape measure before drywall ([[renovation-photo-log]]). Two bars went in during the remodel; a third by the toilet the week after Mom first used the room ([[hall-bathroom-inspection-2026-05-20]]).

Same idea worth copying at Mom's house if it is ever remodeled; her current bars went into studs ([[moms-home-safety-upgrades]]).
